title: STARS: Retrospective analysis of outcomes after end versus loop stoma in individuals with spinal cord injury
summary:
People with spinal cord injury often have major problems with bowel emptying. This can take a great deal of time, lead to accidental stool leakage, and strongly affect daily life and quality of life. In such situations, a bowel stoma may help. However, there is still very little evidence on whether different types of stoma differ in everyday life, complications, and quality of life.
This study therefore aims to investigate whether end stoma and loop stoma differ in people with spinal cord injury. The main focus is on complications, hospital readmissions, additional surgery, effort needed for bowel care, and quality of life. The study will also examine whether the timing of stoma creation influences these outcomes.
This is a single-center observational study. First, medical records of adult patients who received an intestinal stoma at the spinal cord injury center of BG Klinikum Hamburg-Boberg between January 1, 2015 and December 31, 2025 will be reviewed. In addition, living and contactable patients with regular follow-up at the center will be invited to complete a one-time survey about their current daily life, care needs, and quality of life. Completing the questionnaire takes about 15 to 20 minutes.
conditions: Injury of nerves and spinal cord at neck level
Injury of nerves and spinal cord at thorax level
Injury of nerves and lumbar spinal cord at abdomen, lower back and pelvis level
Other injuries of spine and trunk, level unspecified

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years at the time of stoma creation
Confirmed spinal cord injury (traumatic or non-traumatic)
Creation of a permanent or temporary intestinal stoma (colostomy or ileostomy) at the Spinal Cord Injury Center / BG Klinikum Boberg during the defined observation period from 2015-01-01 to 2025-12-31
Complete operative documentation and available baseline data, in particular level of lesion and AIS classification (American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale), where available
Exclusion criteria:
Missing or severely incomplete medical records
Deceased at the time of a potentially planned survey (applies to the questionnaire component of the study)
